items.title: Bill Mays interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 5, 2025
items.q: I did. On a movie that Lalo Schiffrin wrote the score on. It was called “Roller Coaster.”

ctx.x: I did. On a movie that Lalo Schiffrin wrote the score on. It was called “Roller Coaster.” And interestingly the whole score was just for keyboard instruments. I think there were six or seven of us. And pipe organ was on that score too. It was a terrible movie but a great score. But at the same time I was doing studio work I was playing jazz. The only thing I couldn’t really do was go on the road for extended periods of time because as a studio player – then and now – if you get a call with a contractor you want…
And along the way you felt compelled to become a composer. Can I ask you what kind of circumstances you are inspired by to compose something?
